classification: restructures without inventing/replacing financial values (this case: a genuine single-money-column DATE/DESCRIPTION/AMOUNT table with a spilled description column)
what_changes: row 0's DATE.../AMOUNT... fusion (with an unrecognized middle cell that defeats split_fused_header_row) is reconstructed into a clean header + first data row; a later 4-cell row with a spilled description column is collapsed to 3 columns, joining the spill into the description
what_does_not_change: every row's single money value (260.00, 235.17, 450.00) and every date; the already-3-column last row is untouched
semantics_note: the date/digit_run delta is the same classification-boundary artifact as split_fused_header_row's fixture ('04/06' glued to 'DATE' has no word boundary before this census's own date regex; once reconstructed into its own cell the extractor recognizes it). No money value moved to a different transaction row, was deleted, or was invented. This case is the SAFE half of this function -- it never applies to a table with more than one money column per row; see debit_credit_balance_folded for the case where it does not stay safe
